clue.text: Indian city built around old marketplace

indicators.note: built around says the city's letters are put up round another piece

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: An Indian city has grown up around an ancient trading square.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece the agora was the public square where trade and assembly took place.

clue.text: Risk in opening accepted by a painter right away

indicators.note: accepted by says the opening goes inside the following piece
right away says R, for right, is taken off

parts.note: Albrecht Durer was the German painter and engraver
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A gamble involving an opening that a painter took up at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but means drop the abbreviation for right; Albrecht Durer was the German Renaissance artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A venture or hazardous undertaking involves danger, and to risk is to hazard.

clue.text: Stink produced by circular letter not at all pleasant

parts.note: O is the letter shaped like a circle
dour means stern and gloomy

explanation.surface: A fuss caused by a nasty circular letter sent round.
explanation.definitionFit: A stink is a smell, especially an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Friendly colt in friendly environment

indicators.note: in says the letter for colt sits inside the other word

parts.note: amiable means friendly, here the surrounding word
C is the abbreviation for colt in horse-racing form

explanation.surface: A young horse at home in a welcoming setting is friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and good-natured, as when people get along without quarrel.

clue.text: It's not legit, somehow, accepting money like this

definitions.text: It's not legit, somehow, accepting money like this

indicators.note: accepting says the rearranged letters take in another piece
somehow says the letters of these words are worked into some other order

parts.note: L stands for pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Money acquired this way is illicit, gained by some crooked route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges NOT LEGIT, and 'accepting' puts L inside; the whole clue also describes the answer, since money gained dishonestly is not legitimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-gotten money is obtained dishonestly, so it is not legitimately come by.

clue.text: Islands, to differing extents, accommodating black bird

indicators.note: accommodating says those letters take in the letter for black

parts.note: island is shortened to I and islands to IS, two abbreviations of differing length
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Islands of various sizes provide homes for a dark bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to differing extents' asks for two abbreviations of different lengths, I and IS, with B between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill.

clue.text: He may broadcast appalling rubbish!

parts.note: broadcast in its old sense of scatter widely, as one tossing waste in the street does, rather than airing poor programmes

explanation.surface: A complaint about someone putting out dreadful programmes on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for a person who drops waste in public places.

clue.text: A secretive person in Pistol's world

definitions.meaning: someone close and uncommunicative, as close as a shellfish keeps its shell
Pistol in Shakespeare's Merry Wives of Windsor says the world is his for opening with his sword

explanation.walkthrough: Pistol is a character in Shakespeare, not a gun; his line 'the world's mine oyster' gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-lipped person is likened to a shellfish that stays shut, and Pistol calls the world his shellfish to prise open.

clue.text: First-class confection served up outside hill restaurant

indicators.note: outside says these reversed letters go round the hill
served up in a down clue says these letters read upward, so backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here with I for the numeral
a tart is a sweet pastry confection
a tor is a rocky hill in south-west England

explanation.surface: A top-quality dessert brought out at a hillside eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'served up' means read upward; A1, written AI, is the usual crossword spelling of first-class, and a tor is a Dartmoor-style rocky hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an Italian-style eating place, usually simple and informal.

clue.text: Woman in New York who looks after kids?

indicators.note: in says the woman's name sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman in New York employed to care for children.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that a female goat also looks after kids, young goats.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's nurse cares for youngsters, and a female goat tends her young.

clue.text: As Holmes occasionally was, prior to His Last Bow?

definitions.text: As Holmes occasionally was, prior to His Last Bow?

parts.words: As Holmes occasionally was, prior to His Last Bow?
parts.note: Sherlock Holmes played a stringed instrument now and then, and before any final stroke of the bow he would be a player of it; His Last Bow is also a Holmes story title

explanation.surface: A question about the detective's habits before the story His Last Bow.
explanation.walkthrough: His Last Bow is a Sherlock Holmes story; read literally, a bow is what a fiddle player draws across the strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes is known for playing the fiddle, so he was sometimes a string player.

clue.text: Holiday destination popular after spring

indicators.note: after places the word for popular behind the word for spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A fashionable holiday spot follows the spring season.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a country many tourists visit for sun and beaches.

clue.text: Par achieved by woman with new driver

parts.note: Norma is a woman's name
L is the learner plate shown by a new driver in Britain

explanation.surface: A golfer's par score achieved by a woman playing with a new driver club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a golf club alongside 'Par', but a new driver is a learner, whose L-plate gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Par means the usual or average standard, which is what is ordinary.

clue.text: Foreign money deposited in bank not long ago

indicators.note: deposited in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a cent is a coin of foreign currency such as the US dollar

explanation.surface: Someone put foreign currency into a bank just lately.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately or in the near past is what both phrases describe.

clue.text: Misuse a blade when involved in a row

definitions.text: Misuse a blade when involved in a row

parts.words: Misuse a blade when involved in a row
parts.note: the blade is an oar's, and a row is rowing, not a quarrel; mishandling the stroke so the oar jams in the water is the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone wielding a knife badly in the middle of a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: This rowing idiom describes a faulty stroke where the oar sticks in the water.

clue.text: Erratic priest accepted by a Parisian mob half-heartedly

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: accepted by says the priest is taken inside the following piece
half-heartedly says one of the doubled middle letters is lost

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly mob
Eli is the priest in the Bible who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: A wayward priest is taken in by a lukewarm Paris crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' takes away just one of the two middle letters of the mob word, leaving RABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erratic cannot be depended on, its behaviour varying without pattern.

clue.text: Regard one anew as a source of music

indicators.note: anew says the letters of these words are arranged again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Seeing someone afresh as a musical inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium-type instrument that sounds through vibrating metal tongues produces music.

clue.text: The team uttered triumphant cries

definitions.meaning: a group working together, such as a boat's rowers
past tense of crow in its British form, to exult loudly

explanation.definitionFit: A team of workers is a crew, and crew is an old past tense of crow, to shout in triumph.

clue.text: Which food includes English flour?

indicators.note: includes says the pair of words takes in the letter for English

parts.note: what can mean which, as in 'what book?'
a meal is food eaten at one time

explanation.surface: Asking which foodstuff contains English flour.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a brown flour milled from wheat with some bran left in.

clue.text: Carefully consider amount of business done

definitions.meaning: to think about something at length, mulling it over
a firm's total sales over a period

explanation.definitionFit: To mull something is to revolve it in the mind, and a firm's revenue over a year is its sales figure.

clue.text: Flat race, for instance, not quite completed

indicators.note: not quite completed says the final letter is missing

parts.note: a race is an example of a sporting event

explanation.surface: A flat race, such as one held on a horse course, is left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat race' reads as one horse-racing term, but 'Flat' is the definition and 'race, for instance' gives EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means level or smooth, without bumps.

clue.text: Add to mass, involving actual English with Latin included

indicators.note: included says the Latin word is put inside the rearranged letters
involving here means making intricate or tangled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: cum is the Latin word for with

explanation.surface: Building up a mass by mixing real English with a little Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' gives ACULATE from the actual-plus-English letters; 'Add to mass' reads as physics but means amass.
explanation.definitionFit: To pile up more and more is to keep increasing a heap or store.

clue.text: A press chief commissioned it orally, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss gave a commission by word of mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper is its senior journalist.

clue.text: All-embracing method that's associated with American theatres

parts.note: broad means wide-ranging or all-embracing
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A comprehensive approach linked with the theatres of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York street is home to the main commercial theatre district in the USA.

clue.text: Union organisers' statement of intent announced in bars

indicators.note: announced says the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: to bar is to ban or forbid

explanation.surface: Trade union leaders declare their plans in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'union' is a marriage, not a trade union; the organisers are the couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Before a church wedding the couple's intention to marry is read out publicly.

clue.text: One goes round to decorate a low joint

definitions.text: One goes round to decorate a low joint

parts.words: One goes round to decorate a low joint
parts.note: a low joint is the one between leg and foot, and a piece of jewellery worn encircling it decorates it

explanation.surface: Something wrapped round to brighten up a seedy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: This ornament is a band worn around the lower leg just above the foot.

clue.text: Gangling youth knowing nothing about love, initially upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the letters read upward, so backwards
initially says take the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A gawky lad naive about love, at first troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters YKNAL, and 'upset' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangling means tall, thin and awkward-looking.

clue.text: Urgent message about opening of local textile plant

indicators.note: about says the message's letters go round the next piece

parts.note: a fax is a message sent by phone line, used when speed matters

indicators.note: opening of says take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An urgent note concerning the start of a local cloth mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is grown for its fibres, spun into linen.

clue.text: Man of honour executed in hours of darkness

indicators.note: executed here means beheaded, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a knight is a man honoured by the Crown

explanation.surface: A man of honour put to death after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The time between dusk and dawn is when it is dark.

clue.text: Application form for 19 — clear?

indicators.note: form as a verb means shape or make up, so these letters are made into a new word

parts.note: the answer to 19 across is the word for flat or level

explanation.surface: Asking whether an application form is clear for a particular entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Application form' reads as one paperwork phrase; 'form' is the anagram indicator, working on EVEN (the answer to 19) and CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Application can mean bearing on the matter in hand, that is, pertinence.

clue.text: Watch cover

parts.note: a watch is a guard on duty, and a shelter for them gives cover

explanation.definitionFit: This is the small hut that shelters a guard on duty.

clue.text: Return to deposit gold sovereign

indicators.note: return says the whole run of letters is turned round

parts.note: to lay is to deposit or set down
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Give back the gold coin placed on deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' looks like the gold coin, but here it is the adjective meaning regal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovereign as an adjective means kingly, belonging to a monarch.
